Introduced the Aged Care (Accommodation Payment Security) Levy Amendment Bill 2025 to keep registered providers subject to the guarantee scheme under the Aged Care Act 2024 and allow the government to recover guarantee costs from certain providers in circumstances such as a default event.

Supported the aged care amendments but sought Senate inquiries, arguing that 325 changes and 197 repeals require scrutiny and consultation. Reported that grandfathering and the no worse off principle would be protected, while criticising delays to reforms, unreleased rules and the wait for home care packages by more than 87,000 older Australians.
Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, six bills stood referred to the Federation Chamber after debate on their second-reading motions was adjourned.

Presented the Selection of Bills Committee report and moved its adoption, including referrals of aged care, Fair Work and Pacific banking bills; amendments proposed public inquiries into intelligence and Defence Housing Australia bills, and the amended motion was agreed to.

Spoke on two aged-care amendment bills, said they were necessary to deliver the Aged Care Act 2024 and royal commission recommendations, and stated that the coalition would not obstruct passage while criticising the government's implementation and rejection of transitional amendments; debate was interrupted.

Criticised the government's preparation for aged-care reform, arguing that delayed legislation and incomplete systems had left older Australians waiting for assessed care, while supporting the bills as necessary to implement the Aged Care Act 2024, grandfathering arrangements and the no-worse-off principle.
